policy_title: Introduce a Legal Cap on Migration
stated: The Conservative Party will introduce a binding, legal cap on migration, specifically for work and family visas, ensuring that numbers fall every year of the next Parliament to protect public services and housing, with Parliament voting annually on the level.

source.quote: Introduce a legal cap on migration to guarantee that numbers will fall every year, so public services are protected while bringing in the skills our businesses and NHS needs.

bearing_set.reason: A legally binding, falling cap directly constrains net migration demand on housing; the policy explicitly cites housing protection, making supply-demand effects on affordability and availability a core verdict question.

NHS and social care rely heavily on internationally-recruited staff; a binding work-visa cap directly constrains healthcare workforce replenishment, with material consequences for waiting times and capacity.

A cap on work visas restricts labour supply across sectors, producing contested but non-negligible effects on wages, job competition, and conditions for both resident workers and migrant workers legally present.

A binding cap on family visas directly engages Article 8 ECHR rights to family life for UK residents and citizens seeking to bring family members, and may bear disproportionately on particular ethnic communities, placing this squarely within the legal-rights and equal-treatment scope of O9.

The care sector has specifically depended on overseas care workers post-Brexit; capping work visas would directly hit care-worker numbers, moving social care access and care waiting-time indicators materially.

Restricting family visas imposes a state constraint on UK residents' ability to live with foreign-national family members, constituting a concrete restriction on personal life choices and freedom from state coercion.

The Migration Advisory Committee and OBR document that working-age migrants are net fiscal contributors; reducing their numbers alters the tax-revenue-to-public-expenditure ratio, bearing on debt-path sustainability.

A cap on work visas constrains the supply of both high-skilled workers and entrepreneurs, bearing on productivity, business investment, and real living standards — contested in direction and magnitude but mechanistically direct.

Migration volume and pace are primary independent variables in social-trust and integration research; a binding cap explicitly targets the scale of new arrivals and thereby bears on integration outcomes, inter-group contact, and community belonging.

membership_note: Seven fundamentals clear the non-negligible bar because this is a broad cross-cutting instrument that directly touches housing demand, labour supply, healthcare workforce, public finances, personal liberty (family visas), economic capacity, and social integration — all with traceable indicators, not merely vague spillovers.
